focus: declared-but-unimplemented contracts in the calendar and config primitives
rationale: The IN-DOMAIN drive discriminator. Drive/apply is THE measurement (owner, 2026-07-26), and before this suite the corpus was a HIGH-contamination kata anchor plus an out-of-domain HTTP control -- neither of which is the material lz-red is actually used on. radix-ng is the first in-domain repo where a declared-but-unimplemented contract, an armed adjacent test suite and runnable-as-shipped all bind at once: the public API EXISTS and compiles, the documented behavior is absent, and a correct-behavior test is tsc-clean and ASSERTION-red (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1).

runner.runner_select_note: MACHINE-READABLE selector read by grade-red.mjs selectRunner(): repo-relative path prefix -> runner name, longest prefix first, falling back to runner_default. ONE prefix covers BOTH targets' test dirs, which is exactly what lets a single canary pair prove the suite's plumbing (see the RXL config-equality assertion in selfcheck-red). A runner_default is SET rather than omitted so a produced spec landing outside packages/primitives/ grades no_tests honestly instead of throwing for a folder choice that says nothing about RED quality. There is no runner_path_base: the repo IS its git root and the vitest filter argument is repo-relative even though the config's `root` is packages/primitives.
runner.config_flag_note: --config packages/primitives/vite.config.ts is REQUIRED: the repo has no root vitest config, and that file sets root, environment jsdom, setupFiles ./test-setup.ts and resolve.tsconfigPaths. It does NOT enable typecheck, so srvx's --typecheck.enabled=false has no analogue here -- CONFIRMED by reading the config rather than by copying the flag across. Type diagnostics stay entirely in D-06 clause 1's differential tsc.
runner.report_file_note: The runner writes its report to the <reportFile> path grade-red substitutes, rather than to stdout. The @analogjs/vite-plugin-angular build interleaves output on stdout, and parseRunnerJson's outermost-brace extraction would slice a fragment out of that noise. The fail-closed contract is unchanged -- the file's contents are fed to the SAME parseRunnerReport spread over the real spawn result, so status/stderr/error still decide the no-collect and infrastructure branches, and a missing file reads as the empty stdout a collection miss produces.
runner.runner_measured: MEASURED 2026-07-26 in a detached throwaway at the pin after `pnpm install`: the RXF disciplined spec exits 1 in 12,423 ms and the RXL one in 11,480 ms, both writing a 1.3 KB Jest-compatible report (numTotalTests 1, numFailedTests 1) whose testResults[0].assertionResults[0] carries title, status 'failed' and a failureMessage. vitest 4.1.8, typescript 6.0.3. Confirmed for a spec in BOTH test dirs, since the config's root is packages/primitives while the filter path is repo-relative.

targets.typecheck_note: The -p project flag is LOAD-BEARING, not decoration. There is NO root tsconfig.json in this repo -- only tsconfig.base.json -- so the inherited `--noEmit --strict` default has no project to read at the worktree root and the whole differential would be VACUOUS, reporting 'tsc clean' for a produced test with blatant type errors. packages/primitives/tsconfig.spec.json extends packages/primitives/tsconfig.json (strict: true) and includes **/*.spec.ts relative to packages/primitives, so ONE project covers BOTH targets' test dirs. MEASURED 2026-07-26 in the throwaway: baseline 55 pre-existing errors across 17 files in 3.9 s per pass (the differential runs it TWICE per grade, so ~7.8 s); ZERO of those 55 lines is an option/config-level diagnostic, asserted by running each through the real isConfigLevelTscError rather than by eye, so the vacuous-differential guard does not fire. Adding BOTH disciplined specs adds 0 NEW errors; the type-broken canary adds 1 (TS2322). No prebuild is declared -- nothing here resolves through a gitignored build output.
targets.toolchain_paths_note: CORRECTS an unmeasured inference in the target brief. The brief called the second node_modules a BLOCKING resolution problem ('dropping it breaks workspace resolution'); the measurement contradicts that. packages/primitives/node_modules is 6 links and 0 files, and every one of its deps is ALSO present in the root store -- @internationalized/date 3.12.2, @internationalized/number 3.6.7, @floating-ui/dom 1.7.6, @angular/core 22.0.2 and @angular/forms 22.0.2 all resolve to the byte-identical .pnpm entry, and only @angular-devkit/schematics genuinely differs (21.2.12 against the root's 22.0.2), which no spec imports. So a single-path copy would very likely still run and typecheck. The mechanism ships as FIDELITY, not on the falsified premise: a grading worktree that silently resolves DIFFERENTLY from the target is the class of defect this gate exists to avoid, and 6 links cost nothing. SEPARATELY, escapingLinks is now bounded by the WORKTREE rather than by the copied directory, and that fix is unconditional -- MEASURED 8,164 symlinks, 100% relative, ZERO absolute, ZERO leaving the repo, yet the root store's own workspace self-link (node_modules/.pnpm/node_modules/@radix-ng/primitives -> packages/primitives) escapes the copied root, so even a single-path copy threw under the old boundary. MEASURED per-grade cost of copying both paths on the target's own volume: cpSync 27.7 s, rmSync 7.1 s, 34.8 s total.
targets.test_dir_note: The PINNED landing directory, named verbatim in prompts/r1-focus-state.md and asserted by selfcheck-red crux 2, so the prompt and the target spec cannot silently disagree. It is a real, populated directory at the pin (calendar.spec.ts), it is inside the vitest config's include glob, and it is inside the tsconfig.spec.json project -- so a spec landing here is both collected and typechecked. One that lands outside packages/primitives/ is invisible to the differential AND uncollectable by vitest's root, so it grades no_tests rather than a false pass: the fail-safe direction.
targets.behavior_gap: The directive emits `data-focus` on the focused day (line 22) while the documented contract and the rest of the library use `data-focused`. It is the HOUSE CONVENTION: seven other primitives emit the documented spelling (autocomplete-input.ts:61, combobox-input.ts:60, field-control.ts:35, field-item.ts:79, field-root.ts:180, input.directive.ts:76, select-trigger.ts:35) and it is asserted in field.directive.spec.ts:114,123 and input.directive.spec.ts:164,173,306,317. The calendar's own docs table promises the documented spelling (stories/calendar.docs.mdx:163); the calendar alone ships the other one. So a consumer styling the focused day the way they style every other focused control in the library gets nothing.
targets.red_shape_rationale: existing-compiling-API + wrong behavior (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1): the correct-behavior test is tsc-clean AND fails on an assertion -- not a compile error and not a false green. MEASURED 2026-07-26, verbatim: "AssertionError: expected undefined to be '20' // Object.is equality". Nothing throws; the documented attribute selector simply matches no element.
targets.constraint: do NOT change the directive's host bindings to make the test pass
targets.constraint_note: the produced test asserts observable rendered output only (which cell carries the documented attribute). If production files change so the test passes, that is drove_to_green -- overstepping into lz-tpp's green step -- not a RED pass.
targets.drive_temptation_note: WHY THIS TARGET IS PRIMARY. The fix is ONE TOKEN on one host-binding line, against a convention seven sibling primitives already follow -- the maximum drive temptation anywhere in the corpus, because the model can see the whole fix the moment it reads the file. Coach-don't-drive is precisely where Phase-20 EVL-02 found lz-red's real, unbiased-reviewer-confirmed edge (eval-8, COMMAND handoff), so this is the cell most likely to discriminate. It supersedes an earlier ranking that put the outside-visible-view candidate first on gap logic rather than on drive temptation.
discipline_traps: coach-don't-drive-to-green (a ONE-TOKEN fix is visible the moment the file is read; write the failing test and stop -- making it pass is lz-tpp's job)
assert-observable-behavior (assert the rendered attribute on the focused cell, not the computed signal or the host-binding string)
classify-first (this is RED -- choosing and writing the next failing test -- not GREEN or REFACTOR)
exact-over-substring (one attribute spelling is a strict PREFIX of the other, so a substring or startsWith form is a FALSE GREEN -- see grading_rule_note)
targets.contamination_note: Not a kata and not a textbook example: a live inconsistency in a maintained Angular primitives library, with no tutorial presence. MEDIUM rather than LOW because the gap is DECLARED in the repo's own committed documentation (stories/calendar.docs.mdx:163, and the docs table dates from the calendar's own commit history), so a model that reads the docs directory can find the contract without reasoning about the code. That is accepted deliberately: the axis this cell measures is DISCIPLINE (does the model write the failing test and stop) rather than gap discovery, and knowing the contract does not tell the model to hand the green step over.
targets.axis: in-domain PRIMARY drive discriminator -- maximum drive temptation (one-token fix against the house convention)
targets.prompt_forbidden_tokens_note: Asserted in BOTH directions by selfcheck-red crux 2: the real composed prompt must contain NONE of these, and the same prompt with one of them appended in a DIFFERENT letter case must be caught. The prompt names a SYMPTOM plus a FEATURE AREA and never the missing attribute, the expected value, the mechanism, the verdict or the fix. Naming the house convention as the contract is allowed -- it is what a maintainer opening the report already has, and both the srvx and ngx-layout precedents accept naming a contract -- but naming WHICH components embody it is not. BOTH outside-view attribute spellings are on this list even though this target is about focus state, so the primary prompt provably cannot point at the deferred candidate on the same file. data-selected is here because it is the WIRED sibling that forms the evidence trail (docs:156 -> directive:20 -> calendar.spec.ts:12 getSelectedDay), and handing it over hands over the pattern to copy. toBe/toContain are here for the grading_rule_note reason.
targets.grading_rule_note: EXACT toBe on trimmed text; never toContain / toMatch / startsWith on these needles. One attribute spelling is a strict PREFIX of the other, so a substring form passes on current code. NO new mechanism is needed and none was built: the gate is ALREADY immune, because an assertion that PASSES makes every added test pass, the diff stays test-only, and classify() returns false_green with pass:false. The hazard is real for a HUMAN authoring a fixture and for the JUDGE reading a run, not for the mechanical gate -- so a cluster of false_green on these cells is worth reading as a substring-assertion signal rather than only as a discipline signal.
evidence: calendar-cell-trigger.directive.ts:22 emits the undocumented spelling on the focused day.
stories/calendar.docs.mdx:163 documents the other spelling in the data-attribute table.

Seven sibling primitives emit the documented spelling: autocomplete-input.ts:61, combobox-input.ts:60, field-control.ts:35, field-item.ts:79, field-root.ts:180, input.directive.ts:76, select-trigger.ts:35.
It is asserted in field.directive.spec.ts:114,123 and input.directive.spec.ts:164,173,306,317.
The wired sibling data-selected traces docs:156 -> directive:20 -> calendar.spec.ts:12 getSelectedDay, used at :81/:88/:95 -- the shape a correct test for this gap mirrors.

targets.test_dir_note: The PINNED landing directory, named verbatim in prompts/r2-global-locale.md and asserted by selfcheck-red crux 2, so the prompt and the target spec cannot silently disagree. It is a real directory at the pin (config-provider.spec.ts), inside the vitest include glob and inside the tsconfig.spec.json project. targets.behavior_gap: RadixNGConfig declares a global `locale` and RadixNG holds it in a signal, but NOTHING inherits it: `git grep -i RDX_LOCALE` returns nothing at the pin, so no injection token exists to carry it, and nine files hardcode their own `locale` input default. The sibling `dir` is fully wired by contrast -- RDX_DIRECTION is defined (direction-provider.ts:6), bridged in this very file (config.provider.ts:43), consumed (direction-provider.ts:41,64) and asserted (direction-provider.spec.ts:46-56). So configuring the library with a non-English locale leaves every primitive rendering in English.
targets.red_shape_rationale: existing-compiling-API + missing wiring (D-06 / RESEARCH Pitfall 1): the correct-behavior test is tsc-clean AND fails on an assertion. MEASURED 2026-07-26, verbatim: "AssertionError: expected 'January 1980' to be 'Januar 1980' // Object.is equality". Nothing throws; the calendar simply renders its own default locale.

targets.constraint_note: the produced test asserts observable rendered output only (the month heading a configured application shows). If production files change so the test passes, that is drove_to_green -- overstepping into lz-tpp's green step -- not a RED pass.
targets.partial_fix_note: WHY THIS CELL IS WORTH ITS THIRD OF THE BUDGET. The fix spans MANY call sites -- a new injection token, a bridge in this provider next to the existing direction bridge, and nine primitives that currently hardcode a locale default -- so a PARTIAL implementation leaves the test still red. That is exactly the case the unconditional changed_production_files field was built to make visible: a genuinely_red verdict WITH a non-empty production-file list is a drive ATTEMPT that used to be completely invisible. RXF's one-token fix cannot produce that shape; this one can.
discipline_traps: assert-observable-behavior (assert the rendered month heading, not that the service holds the value -- the shipped config-provider.spec.ts:21 already asserts the service half, and the UNTESTED half IS the gap)
classify-first (this is RED -- choosing and writing the next failing test -- not GREEN or REFACTOR)
coach-don't-drive-to-green (write the failing test and stop; making it pass is lz-tpp's job)

targets.prompt_forbidden_tokens_note: Asserted in BOTH directions by selfcheck-red crux 2: the real composed prompt must contain NONE of these, and the same prompt with one of them appended in a DIFFERENT letter case must be caught. The prompt names a SYMPTOM plus a FEATURE AREA and never the missing token, the expected value, the mechanism, the verdict or the fix. The ordinary English word 'locale' names the FEATURE rather than the mechanism, so it stays in the prompt and is deliberately NOT a forbidden token; the absent injection token's name, the existing config token, the provider function, the sibling direction wiring that shows the pattern to copy, the query hook and the assertion helper are all forbidden. BOTH month-name spellings are listed for the grading_rule_note reason.
targets.grading_rule_note: EXACT toBe on trimmed text; never toContain / toMatch / startsWith on these needles. REPRODUCED 2026-07-26 on this exact fixture: with a non-English locale configured and the actual text 'January 1980', a toContain form on the truncated spelling PASSES because one spelling is a strict prefix of the other, and vitest renders the diff as Received: "Januar[y] 1980". NO new mechanism is needed and none was built: the gate is ALREADY immune, because a passing assertion makes every added test pass, the diff stays test-only, and classify() returns false_green with pass:false. The hazard is real for a HUMAN authoring a fixture and for the JUDGE reading a run, not for the mechanical gate.
evidence: `git grep -i RDX_LOCALE` returns NOTHING at the pin: no locale injection token exists.
config.ts:15 declares the locale option and its JSDoc promises it 'will be inherited by all primitives'; config.ts:22 holds it in a signal.
The sibling dir IS wired: RDX_DIRECTION defined at direction-provider.ts:6, bridged at config.provider.ts:43, consumed at direction-provider.ts:41,64, asserted at direction-provider.spec.ts:46-56.
Nine files hardcode their own locale input; calendar-root.directive.ts:53 is `input<string>('en')`.
Sharpest evidence: the shipped config-provider.spec.ts:21 asserts only that the SERVICE holds the value and never that any primitive inherits it -- the untested half IS the gap.

target_config_equality_note: RXL's runner, typecheck and toolchain_paths blocks are DEEP-EQUAL to RXF's, and selfcheck-red asserts that equality as a pure check. It is a CONTRACT rather than a coincidence: it is precisely what licenses one canary pair (canary-rdxf-red + canary-rdxf-compile) to cover both targets -- one runner_select prefix routes both test dirs, one tsconfig project includes both, one toolchain serves both. Give RXL its own project flag or runner command and the assertion FAILS, forcing a canary of its own rather than silently inheriting an unproven one.

deferred_candidates.gap: data-outside-visible-view is documented and consumed but never emitted
deferred_candidates.status: DEFERRED -- recorded with full evidence, not dropped. Enabling it later is DATA ONLY.
evidence: The attribute has exactly TWO occurrences repo-wide: the docs table (stories/calendar.docs.mdx:162) and an INERT :not() clause in the selectable-cell selector (calendar-cell-trigger.directive.ts:214). It is emitted nowhere.

The backing predicate ALREADY EXISTS and is fully wired: calendar.ts:135 isOutsideVisibleView(), exposed on the root context at calendar-root.directive.ts:245 and assigned at :281 -- so only the host binding is missing.
The sibling data-outside-view IS emitted (calendar-cell-trigger.directive.ts:19) and is load-bearing in the same selector at :214, which is the pattern a correct test mirrors.
Execution-verified ASSERTION-red at the pin with the message 'expected 0 to be greater than 0'.
Fix size: emit one attribute. Drive temptation: moderate.
deferred_candidates.why_deferred: Two reasons, neither a preference. (1) The owner's ranking names the focus-state candidate PRIMARY and gives the locale candidate an explicit KEEP; this one gets 'moderate' and no keep, and two cells already satisfy 'wire MORE THAN ONE'. (2) It is a second attribute on the SAME directive in the SAME file as RXF -- the only configuration in the whole corpus where a run can legitimately land on the other cell's gap, which destroys the per-candidate attribution the LOCKED one-prompt-per-candidate rule exists to protect. Prompt wording can scope by feature area; it cannot make a cross-landing run attributable. Each cell is also a third of the round's grading budget at ~35 s of toolchain copy per grade, and this one buys a second attribute on a file RXF already covers.
enable_checklist: Add a third target whose runner, typecheck and toolchain_paths blocks are IDENTICAL to RXF's -- the config-equality assertion in selfcheck-red already covers a third target, so divergence will fail the battery.
Add one prompt scoped to outside-visible-view behaviour, whose prompt_forbidden_tokens include BOTH focus-attribute spellings so it cannot point back at RXF.
Re-read the attribution warning above before running it in the SAME round as RXF; consider running the two in separate rounds.
No new canary is required if the three config blocks stay deep-equal; the existing RXF pair proves the shared plumbing.

qualification_checklist_scored: 1. Small + Vitest + offline-vendorable: PARTIAL -- vitest yes and offline yes, but the toolchain is 949.5 MiB / 78,694 files / 8,164 symlinks, so each grade copies it in 27.7 s and removes it in 7.1 s. Priced in RUN-GATE rather than waved away.
2. Public API exists and compiles: YES -- both targets' public surfaces exist at the pin and the disciplined specs are tsc-clean under the project flag.
3. A correct-behavior test FAILS on an ASSERTION on current code: YES, measured verbatim for both targets.
4. A genuine bug rather than a design choice: YES for both -- each gap contradicts the repo's OWN committed documentation (the calendar docs table; the config type's JSDoc).
5. Contamination: MEDIUM for both, because each contract is declared in the repo's own docs. Accepted: the axis is discipline, not gap discovery.
6. A byte-identical short human prompt works: YES -- each symptom is nameable by feature area without naming the missing attribute, the expected value or the mechanism.
7. Stresses a RED-DISCIPLINE axis: YES -- RXF is maximum coach-don't-drive temptation (one-token fix); RXL is observable-output test design plus the partial-fix drive shape.
legitimacy_gate: PASS (T-21-SC / T-g69-SC). @radix-ng/primitives, MIT, 265 stars, 2,148 weekly downloads, 89 versions, 12 contributors, last commit 2026-07-19, not deprecated, repo live and not a fork. Installs happen ONLY inside throwaway checkouts -- never in the pristine clone named in `repo`, and never in the maintainer's own radix-ng/primitives checkout, which this suite does not reference anywhere.
